title: Christmas Day: The Word Made Flesh
paragraphs: And there, in Bethlehem, Mary's baby was born. She wrapped him in cloths and laid him in a manger, a feeding trough, because there was no other bed. The shepherds arrived, breathless, and found everything just as they had been told. They knelt, and then they went out singing, telling everyone what they had seen. Mary quietly treasured it all in her heart. John's Gospel tells it in the biggest words: in the beginning was the Word, and the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not put it out. "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us" (KJV). The first light, the thread, the promise: here, a baby, God with us. Happy Christmas.
wonder: I wonder what it means that the light of the world came as a baby?
activity: Gather around a crib or a candle, light it, and tell the whole thread of the story back from Day 1 in your own words.
prayer: Child of Bethlehem, light of the world, be born in our hearts today and make us bearers of your light. Amen.
alt: A manger glows at the centre of a stable, wrapped in a golden thread, with a star above and watchers kneeling.
hidden: Look for every hidden detail from the 24 earlier days gathered in this picture (owl, dove, lamb, harp, etc.). A "find them all" challenge.
translation: Retold in our own words, with a short quotation from the King James Version.
